michelle: Heads up — after the kernel-selection change that landed last night we're seeing p99 tail latency up ~18% for EU customers when load is medium-high. traces point to longer queue waits, not token gen. suspect continuous-batching + cross-zone spill behavior.

arjun: ok can you paste the perf profile + kv cache stats? also which model variant / seq len distribution?

michelle: model: gpt-open-13b-q4 (served as compat fallback), seq hist: 8/32/128 (p25/p50/p75). kv-cache hitrate: 72% eu-east, 59% eu-west. profiler excerpt below (flame summary):
```
30%  runtime::batch_formation::wait_loop
22%  runtime::kernel_sel::select_path (switch for short seqs)
15%  runtime::kv_cache::lookup (miss path hot)
10%  runtime::scheduler::crosszone_spill
23%  other
```

michelle: observed queue depth spikes coincide with crosszone spill events (eu-west -> eu-east), looks like bursty handoffs causing backpressure.

leo: hmm kernel_sel switching for short seqs + batching waits is suspicious — we may be forcing a kernel change mid-batch which increases startup cost. try increasing the kernel-stability threshold for batches < 64 tokens.

arjun: agree. also we should revisit token-budget allocation per-region. right now global token budget is 120 tokens/batch and we do soft-share across zones. when eu-west spills, eu-east accepts but then its token budget is temporarily saturated, causing long tail for new requests.

kai: proposed quick config tweak to test: turn on strict-affinity for eu zones (allow spill only if local queue > 200ms) and lower global token target to 100. patch:
```
# runtime queue policy
regions:
  eu:
    affinity: strict
    spill_threshold_ms: 200
global:
  continuous_batching_token_target: 100
  kernel_stability_min_tokens: 64
```

jana: i'll run a canary with that config on staging. also want to add instrumentation to record per-batch kernel_id so we can see if kernel switches correlate with lane handoffs.

michelle: thanks. one more datapoint — when we disabled crosszone spill in a short A/B test yesterday tail dropped ~12% but throughput fell ~6% (under heavy load). so there's a latency/cost tradeoff.

leo: that's expected. my hypothesis: we can get most of the latency win by avoiding spill for small/short requests while still allowing spill for large long-running streams. add a policy: allow-spill-if-estimated-runtime > 80ms.

arjun: good call. we can estimate runtime from tokens * mean per-token-cost by kernel. we'll add a fast estimator in scheduler.

kai: logs from last 10m showing spill events and token budgets: 
```
[10:12:01] eu-west: queue_len=34 token_budget=18 spill_out=12 -> eu-east
[10:12:01] eu-east: accept_spill=12 token_budget=0 queue_wait_avg=245ms
[10:12:07] eu-west: queue_len=8 token_budget=90
[10:12:07] eu-east: kernel_switch=true batch_tokens=28 startup_ms=18
```

jana: test plan I'm going to run tonight:
- stage canary (10% traffic) with kai's strict-affinity + token_target=100
- track p50/p95/p99 by region, kv hitrate, kernel-switch-rate, spill-accept count
- run separate canary with leo's estimated-runtime spill rule
- compare throughput and cost per token

michelle: perfect. if canaries look good we can roll to EU with a 30min canary and circuit-breaker to revert on p99 regressions > 10%.

sre-bot: deploy scheduled: canary config push to staging at 2026-07-12T02:00:00Z (canary id c-3319).

arjun: action items: 
- jana/kai: run canaries + upload CSVs (p50,p95,p99,kernel-switch,kv-hitrate) — due EOD PST
- leo: prototype estimator for estimated-runtime (PR incoming)
- michelle: gather logs for previous rollback attempt (so we can check if earlier kernel rollouts had same pattern)

michelle: thx all, will post results here. :thumbsup:
